literal: From flaw completely separated people of vision eat not from life completely separated flesh.
translation: People of clear vision, who are completely separated from flaws, will not eat flesh that is separated from life.
modern: குற்றங்களிலிருந்து முழுமையாக நீங்கிய தெளிவான அறிவை உடையவர்கள், உயிரிலிருந்து பிரிக்கப்பட்ட ஊனை உண்ண மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet draws a poetic and moral parallel between the purity of the eater and the nature of the food. The word 'ceyir' means a flaw or blemish; those who have separated themselves from such moral flaws possess clear vision and understanding. Just as these wise individuals are separated from faults, meat is simply flesh that has been separated from life. Recognizing this grim reality, people of flawless understanding will refuse to consume the dead flesh of another creature.
